title: Depth analysis of the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm with a Grover mixer
abstract: We study the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm with a Grover mixer and independently sampled cost and mixing angles. Under a lattice condition on the cost values carried by the initial state, we prove a depth-independent lower bound for the variance of the loss at every depth, together with the same bound for the derivative with respect to the final mixing angle. The estimate is instance-dependent and, for fixed locality, is inverse polynomial in the number of qubits for integer-valued local objective functions with uniformly bounded local terms, in particular for MaxCut. We also establish Grover-type reachability bounds showing that the depth required to approximate a prescribed carried eigenspace is bounded below by a constant multiple of the inverse square root of its initial probability.
summary: This theoretical paper analyzes the performance limits of the Grover-mixer enhanced QAOA by deriving depth-independent lower bounds on the loss variance. It proves that achieving high fidelity requires a minimum circuit depth related to the initial state's probability weight. The results are significant for understanding the finite-depth scaling of quantum optimization algorithms.
main_problem: The paper analyzes the depth-dependence of the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) when enhanced with a Grover mixer (GM-QAOA). It seeks to establish finite-depth lower bounds on the variance of the loss function and the depth required for state approximation.
main_result: The authors derive a depth-independent lower bound for the variance of the loss ($	ext{Var}[\ell_p]$) and establish Grover-type reachability bounds showing that the required depth scales inversely with the square root of the initial probability.
method: The analysis uses spectral decomposition of the cost Hamiltonian and develops recursive relations for expected overlaps and variances by averaging over the independently sampled cost and mixing angles.
model_or_system: The model is the GM-QAOA circuit, which alternates between cost evolution ($e^{-i\gamma H}$) and Grover-mixer evolution ($e^{-i eta G}$). The analysis focuses on the dynamics within an invariant subspace defined by the initial state $|\xiangle$.
key_observables: Variance of the loss ($	ext{Var}[\ell_p]$), fidelity of state approximation, and the required circuit depth ($p$).
important_parameters: Lattice spacing ($\eta$), number of qubits ($n$), number of distinct eigenvalues ($d$), and the depth ($p$).
main_assumptions: The analysis critically assumes a lattice condition on the cost eigenvalues ($\lambda_j - \lambda_k \in \eta\mathbb{Z}$) and that the cost and mixing angles are sampled uniformly and independently.
figures_summary: Figures schematically illustrate the GM-QAOA circuit depth, show the attainment of the Grover envelope for specific spectra, and plot numerically found minimum infidelities ($p^*$) against theoretical lower bounds.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by first establishing the variance lower bound (Theorem 1.1) based on spectral properties, followed by deriving the reachability bound (Theorem 1.2). Later sections refine these bounds, analyzing the obstruction to exact state approximation based on the structure of the carried spectrum.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous, finite-depth lower bounds on the performance of QAOA variants, which is crucial for understanding the limitations of quantum optimization algorithms beyond asymptotic analysis.
